issues.description: When client_id is None, last_probe_time is set but no frame is sent. This means the probe timer is 'consumed' without probing. In practice this is benign because stale detection requires last_status_time to be Some (i.e., we've received at least one status), which implies registration has completed and client_id should be Some. But there's a theoretical window between status reception and client_id assignment (or after NewClientQuery resets client_id) where probes would silently do nothing. The old code also had this issue (it sent a hardcoded frame independent of client_id), so this is not a regression.

codeReview.summary: Clean, minimal change that correctly replaces ConfigurationRequest with NothingToSend in the stale probe path. 4 well-structured tests cover all 4 validation assertions. Tests follow TDD (written first, verified to fail, then implementation added). Code follows existing patterns (same NothingToSend usage as in Ready handler at line 696).

issues.description: last_probe_time is unconditionally set even when client_id is None (no frame sent). Pre-existing behavior, not a regression.

summary: PASS. The stale probe in SpaApp::tick() was correctly changed from ConfigurationRequest [0x0A, 0xBF, 0x04] to NothingToSend { client_id }, which is a lightweight no-op command already used elsewhere in the codebase (Ready handler). The 5s probe interval (STALE_PROBE_INTERVAL_MS) and 30s stale threshold (STALE_THRESHOLD_MS) are unchanged. 4 new tests directly verify all 4 validation assertions (VAL-CORE-006 through VAL-CORE-009), and all 6 stale-related tests pass (2 pre-existing + 4 new). The worker followed the rust-worker skill procedure (TDD: tests first, then implementation) and the handoff confirms zero regressions across 442 workspace tests. One minor non-blocking observation: last_probe_time is set even when client_id is None, but this is pre-existing behavior and practically benign.
